newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse trade strongly ahead.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse trade strongly ahead.

text.p: German shares ended electronic trade on Friday up 1.5 percent, having recouped losses from Thursday, but dealers expected the market to take a breather in coming weeks to allow fundamental factors to catch up.
The IBIS DAX index, which monitors trade in 30 blue-chip German stocks, ended at 2,863.26 points, up 42.45 points or 1.50 percent, more than making up for Thursday's drop.
Earlier the DAX-30 index ended bourse trade at 2,859.28 points, up 10.51.

"The market is going to stay volatile next week, but I would stick with sideways volatility. Fundamentals have to catch up with the market after the bull-run of recent weeks," said one Frankfurt trader.
One of the main factors behind Friday's recovery was the fact that Wall Street had a late rally on Thursday.

"People were happy that Wall Street didn't go badly," said the trader. Wall Street proceeded to open higher on Friday afternoon, and was nearly one percent higher at 6,502.53 points as the IBIS DAX index closed.
The other main factor underpinning the market was the strength of the debt market, with Bunds firming throughout the afternoon.
The dollar also lifted German stocks as it continued to strengthen against the mark over the day, to stand at 1.5565/75 marks as IBIS trade ended.

For next week, traders were expecting the market to find support at around 2,800 points, with resistance pegged at around 2,860 points, and did not rule out the possibility of 30-point fluctuations every day.

Most market players would be back from holiday by next week. Looking at individual sectors, dealers were forecasting a possible move out of the chemical sector into cyclical stocks, such as engineering stocks or construction stocks.
Dealers said domestic fund managers were helping underpin the market as they bought up German blue-chips in a bid to increase their German equity weightings early in the year.

Chemical stocks profited from the strengthening dollar, with Bayer AG ending up 80 pfennigs at 61.95 marks, BASF AG ending up 1.81 marks at 58.80 marks and Hoechst AG ending up 78 pfennigs at 70.50 marks.
The financial sector also saw a lot of what volume there was in a relatively thin market, particularly the three major banks.
Commerzbank AG ended up 1.74 marks at 40 marks, Deutsche Bank AG ended up 59 pfennigs at 71.64 marks and Dresdner Bank AG ended up 1.11 pfennigs at 45.72 marks.
